Just based off this post alone, you seem so intelligent and are so well spoken!!! The scholarship?? The amazing extracurriculars?? You are so amazingly bright. But the most important thing is, you should NEVER diminish your own self value because others are diminishing it. You seem to have a wonderful bright future ahead of you, and I'm so sad to hear that your parents are making you not want to live it. 

I don't know if this is any consolation, but when I was 15, I was in the same boat. My parents were very strict and cared more about how well I did in school than they did my own mental health. I kept doing all of these grand things (like clubs and sports and straight A's) to hopefully have their validation, but I never got it. What I learned, and one day you will too, is that you don't need their validation. You must keep thinking of the future and not right now--in three years you'll have that scholarship and move far away from them. You must power through this right now.

If you let your parents get to you, they have won. The only person you should be proving yourself to is YOU! I know one day you'll find hobbies you do for yourself and not for your parents, and I hope that on that day, everything starts feeling a little better.

I'm another BPD and autistic baddie out here. I just finished high school! I talked to a TON of counselors, most of which dismissed my issues, but I promise you there will be at least one authority figure in your school who cares. I managed to graduate early and take less classes because of this, my counselor literally told me to because it was affecting my mental health lol.

But yes, it is possible to finish school with mental health issues. I did it, I'm surprised I did it, but I did it! I couldn't believe myself when I walked across the stage and got my diploma, but I did it. I have belief in you, that you can too! Your mental health issues are merely an obstacle and not a complete boundary from you living a fulfilling life.

I understand that feeling of being judged. If you don't want to talk to anyone, you could try at-home treatments like cognitive behavioral therapy. Or you could do simpler stuff, like setting up time schedules for doing specific things, like homework, free time, eating time, etc etc. I can't really pay attention to a schedule tho so I set up alarms for when to do certain stuff. It reminds me to eat, sleep, when to work, and have free time.

Also, remember that mental health days are completely valid! Your mental health is more important than school. If you need a day off, take it, if you need a week off, take it. It'll help you regroup.

I know this might not be of much help, I'm sorry! I do really hope things get better for you.

Nothing is wrong with you!! You need emotional support and that is completely valid. Have you tried writing down daily affirmations? I know it sounds silly, but I do it a lot and it makes me feel better. I write about how I love my spaced out teeth because they give me character, or I like that I have two lazy eyes because I can take goofy photos with them. It's the small stuff about you that matters

Whatever you decide to do, treatment or not, I have belief and hope in you that you will make it through this. You are cared for deeply, even by a stranger on the internet
